title: Business Cycles
tagline: Business-cycle facts, real business cycles, nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian model, monetary policy rules, the zero lower bound, financial frictions and fiscal stabilisation
summary: Why do economies go through booms and recessions, and what can policy do about them? This course measures business cycles, builds the dynamic models used to explain them — the real business cycle model and the New Keynesian model with sticky prices — and uses them to study monetary policy: interest-rate rules and inflation targeting, the zero lower bound and unconventional policy, the role of financial frictions, and fiscal policy over the cycle.

chapters.title: Measuring business cycles
chapters.summary: Detrending, the cyclical behaviour of output, employment, consumption, investment and prices, and the dating of recessions.

chapters.title: The real business cycle model
chapters.summary: A dynamic general equilibrium model with technology shocks, labour supply and capital accumulation, and how well it fits the data.

chapters.title: Nominal rigidities
chapters.summary: Menu costs, staggered price setting, Calvo pricing, and why money is not neutral in the short run.

chapters.title: The New Keynesian model
chapters.summary: The dynamic IS curve, the New Keynesian Phillips curve and an interest-rate rule in the three-equation model.

chapters.title: Monetary policy rules and inflation targeting
chapters.summary: The Taylor rule and the Taylor principle, inflation targeting, credibility and the time-inconsistency problem.

chapters.title: The zero lower bound and unconventional policy
chapters.summary: Liquidity traps, forward guidance, quantitative easing and negative interest rates.

chapters.title: Financial frictions and the business cycle
chapters.summary: The financial accelerator, credit cycles and the macroeconomics of financial crises.

chapters.title: Fiscal policy over the cycle
chapters.summary: Automatic stabilisers, fiscal multipliers in theory and evidence, and the interaction of fiscal and monetary policy.
